title: Importance of Reciting Salawat on Friday
summary: Discusses the virtues of sending blessings on the Prophet, especially on Friday.
translation: Tonight is the night of Friday. One of the blessings of Friday is that we use its time in the best possible way, and the best thing to do is to present Salawat upon the Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) abundantly. Given the changing circumstances, we are uncertain about tomorrow's events. Our prayer is that Allah makes the future better than the past. However, we are also responsible for trying our best, including frequently reciting Salawat. Insha'Allah, reciting Salawat will make decisions for improving the world's circumstances, and we will see its blessings in our lives, environment, society, country, and especially the entire Islamic world. Thus, reciting Salawat once can decide goodness for several things and the entire Ummah. This is an act in which Allah Himself is involved. When we pray or fast, we do it alone, but Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O believers, send blessings and peace upon him as mentioned in Surah Ahzab. In this verse, Allah attributes Salawat firstly to Himself, then to His luminous creation—the angels, and then commands the believers to send Salawat. Reciting Salawat upon the Prophet brings many blessings, goodness, and safety into our lives. Imam Nasa'i narrates from Abdullah bin Abi Talha from his father that the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) once appeared with signs of joy on his face. When asked about his happiness, he replied that Gabriel had come to him and said, "O Muhammad, are you not pleased that whenever someone sends blessings on you, Allah sends ten blessings upon them, and whenever someone sends peace upon you, Allah sends ten pieces of peace upon them?" Similarly, Abu Hurairah narrates that the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) said that whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends ten blessings upon them. Anas narrates that the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) said that whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send ten blessings, forgive ten sins, and elevate ten ranks for them. According to a Hadith in Jami' Tirmidhi narrated by Abdullah bin Masood, the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) said that those who will be closest to me on the Day of Judgment are those who frequently send Salawat upon me. Many angels travel the earth conveying my Ummah's peace to me. Encourage excessive recitation of Salawat: three thousand, five thousand, ten thousand, or a hundred thousand. Set a target and involve your family and children in achieving that target. Indeed, the best Salawat is the Salawat Ibrahimi: "Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa 'ala Aali Muhammad kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala Aali Ibrahima, innaka Hamidun Majeed. Allahumma barik 'ala Muhammad wa 'ala Aali Muhammad kama barakta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala Aali Ibrahima, innaka Hamidun Majeed." These are the words beloved by the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and were ordained by Allah to be recited in prayer. Therefore, we should aim to recite this Salawat as much as possible because it includes the most excellent phrases. Other forms of Salawat are also permissible to recite.
